The first two statements establish that oranges cost more than apples (O > A) and oranges cost less than bananas (O < B). This implies bananas cost more than oranges (B > O) and, by transitivity, bananas cost more than apples (B > A). The third statement asserts exactly these two relationships: "Bananas cost more than apples and bananas cost more than orange." Both parts are logically entailed by the first two statements, so the third statement is true. Assistant A incorrectly claims it is false, while Assistant B correctly identifies it as true with proper reasoning.
